WHO-IRIS, declared as an INSTANTIATED harness. Owner, 2026-09-21: "who-iris is supposed to be a harness becuase it serves up a new landing page (the iris home page), and has its own docs. it should have who-iris.config.json". Bean zj6c.

THE PRESENCE OF THIS FILE IS THE WHOLE CHANGE. `who-iris/who-iris.json` already declares the instance, and `harness-tiles.ts` already resolved it to `href: /who-iris/` with `hrefKind: "folio"` — its own themed root, because it has its own `docs/`. What it lacked was the second, separate fact: `harness.json` says what an instance DECLARES, and `<name>.config.json` at the instantiation root says the instance is instantiated HERE. Without this file who-iris sorted into the Dependencies group, which is why it was not among the three tabs under HARNESSES.

NAMED FOR THE INSTANCE, not for the directory, and the two happen to agree here. `check:instance-config` verifies the filename names a declared instance; the 2026-09-20 incident it exists for was `folio-assistant.config.json` sitting in `cat-harness/` and silently attaching the platform's configuration to the checkout.
_contentType_comment: `document` rather than `paper`: who-iris is a catalogue of WHO publications and the prose around it — structured prose, no Lean siblings, nothing that reaches pdflatex. Declaring `paper` would scope the paper adapter's LaTeX-shaped QA axes onto content that can never satisfy them, which is the failure `cat-harness.config.json` records against itself. It also picks the MCP adapter (`src/index.ts`), so this drops the Lean and LaTeX tool groups — correct here, where there is no Lean to build.
